title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer thresholds and stabilize regional failover ordering
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: Production incidents over the past week showed the SLO enforcer occasionally over-shedding under transient region errors and entering unstable backoff ordering during simultaneous region evictions. This caused higher-than-expected client error rates and triggered noisy failovers. This hotfix tightens the SLO enforcer thresholds, adds a stable ordering guard for regional failover decisions, and changes the circuit-breaker state transitions to prefer short backoff ramps before full shedding. Changes are intentionally conservative and feature-flagged for rapid rollback. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure mode in perf-canary lab - [x] Add threshold smoothing and ordering guard - [x] Add unit + integration tests for ordering and backoff transitions - [x] Soft rollout to canary, monitor metrics for 6 hours - [x] Global rollout with 1h watch and alert suppression during migration Summary of changes: - SLO enforcer: reduce sensitivity window from 60s -> 45s and add exponential smoothing factor (alpha=0.25) to computed error_rate. - Circuit breaker: add terminal-state guard to ensure we prefer transient backoff (max 3 backoff steps) before entering full load-shedding for a region. - Regional failover: introduce deterministic tie-breaker using region priority + last-success timestamp to avoid oscillatory ordering. - Observability: emit new metrics slo_enforcer.smoothing.alpha and slo_enforcer.tie_breaker.reason; add tracing span when failover ordering is computed. - Feature flag: rollout under feature flag ff:slo_enforcer_tightening with default OFF for non-production. Impact and rollback: expected safer failover ordering, fewer noisy failovers and less aggressive global shedding. Rollback via FF or revert commit if regressions observed. Related tickets/linear: ENG-2142, ENG-2970.
